name: Nebraska

events.title: Statehood
events.text: Nebraska became the 37th state on March 1, 1867. Congress gave it 1 seat in the House until the next apportionment.

events.title: 1870 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1870 census, Nebraska kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1880 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1880 census, Nebraska's House delegation grew from 1 to 3 seats.

events.title: 1890 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1890 census, Nebraska's House delegation grew from 3 to 6 seats.

events.title: 1900 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1900 census, Nebraska kept 6 seats in the House.

events.title: 1910 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1910 census, Nebraska kept 6 seats in the House.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, Nebraska's House delegation shrank from 6 to 5 seats.

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, Nebraska's House delegation shrank from 5 to 4 seats.

events.title: 1950 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1950 census, Nebraska kept 4 seats in the House.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, Nebraska's House delegation shrank from 4 to 3 seats.

events.title: Exon v. Tiemann
events.text: On November 22, 1967, a three-judge federal court held Nebraska's existing congressional districting law invalid. The court reviewed the legislature's replacement three-district law (LB 1) in a February 1968 opinion.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, Nebraska kept 3 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1980 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1980 census, Nebraska kept 3 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1990 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1990 census, Nebraska kept 3 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 2000 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2000 census, Nebraska kept 3 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 2010 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2010 census, Nebraska kept 3 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Special-session map keeps Douglas County whole
events.text: In a 2021 special session, a proposal splitting Douglas County (Omaha) between districts failed to overcome a filibuster. The enacted plan, LB 1, kept Douglas County in the 2nd District, split Sarpy County, and was signed September 30, 2021.

events.title: 2020 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2020 census, Nebraska kept 3 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c048.text: New map drawn after the 1880 census, which raised Nebraska's seats from 1 to 3. It was first used in the 1882 election.

c053.text: New map drawn after the 1890 census, which raised Nebraska's seats from 3 to 6. It was first used in the 1892 election.

c073.text: New map drawn after the 1930 census, which cut Nebraska's seats from 6 to 5. It was first used in the 1932 election.

c078.text: New map drawn after the 1940 census, which cut Nebraska's seats from 5 to 4. It was first used in the 1942 election.

c088.text: New map drawn after the 1960 census, which cut Nebraska's seats from 4 to 3. It was first used in the 1962 election.

c091.text: Nebraska's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1968 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c098.text: New map drawn after the 1980 census, which left Nebraska with 3 seats. It was first used in the 1982 election.

c103.text: New map drawn after the 1990 census, which left Nebraska with 3 seats. It was first used in the 1992 election.

c108.text: New map drawn after the 2000 census, which left Nebraska with 3 seats. It was first used in the 2002 election.

c113.text: New map drawn after the 2010 census, which left Nebraska with 3 seats. It was first used in the 2012 election.

c118.text: New map following: Special-session map keeps Douglas County whole. In a 2021 special session, a proposal splitting Douglas County (Omaha) between districts failed to overcome a filibuster. The enacted plan, LB 1, kept Douglas County in the 2nd District, split Sarpy County, and was signed September 30, 2021.
